rulings.Case Title: JOSEPH ADCOCK VS. THE COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO, A GOVERNMENT ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For A Protective Order Regarding Plaintiffs Discovery Requests
rulings.Rulings: On the Law and Motion/Discovery calendar for September 16, 2026, line 6. DEFENDANT CITY AND COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO'S Motion for a Protective Order Regarding Plaintiffs Discovery Requests. Defendant City and County of San Francisco's motion for a protective order regarding plaintiff's discovery requests and for monetary sanctions is denied. No later than September 30, 2026 the City must serve by email verified code-compliant responses to all of plaintiff Joseph Adcock's second sets of discovery and produce all responsive non-privileged documents in its possession, custody or control. Any information or documents withheld on the grounds of privilege must be identified in a privilege log, which must also be served by e-mail no later than September 30, 2026. The City's multiple technical non-substantive grounds to avoid responding to Adcock's second sets of discovery lack merit given the undisputed facts that the discovery was received by the office of its counsel on August 20 and by the counsel assigned to this case on August 24. The purpose of civil discovery is to allow the parties to learn the facts known and contentions made by the other parties to the lawsuit. Adcock's second sets of discovery are in aid of that important purpose, while the City's motion, in the absence of any identified prejudice from the de minimis technical errors which they attribute to Adcock, is in derogation of that purpose. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept301tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/HEK)
